newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit firms on dollar sales, gains capped.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit firms on dollar sales, gains capped.

text.p: * Ringgit firmed on dollar sales after news of Bank Negara launching attack on currency speculators
* Gains capped by dollar demand by U.S. funds
* Ringgit seen rangebound due to lack of fresh factors

The ringgit firmed in early Asian trading on dollar sales by local and offshore players following a news report that Malaysia's central bank has launched an attack on currency speculators, dealers said.
"Sydney and then local players sold the dollar after a newswire report that Bank Negara has warned banks about speculative trading," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
The report was based on the meeting between Bank Negara and chief executives of some banks last week. The central bank did not make any announcement after the meeting.
But dealers said players were now wondering whether the report was true.
"It was just a repeat of what was reported earlier. It is not something new that you can trade on," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
Some dealers have expressed skepticism about the possibility for Bank Negara to impose some foreign exchange restrictions like those of Thailand.
At 0330 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5095/05 a dollar against 2.5151/61 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
Dealers said dollar buying interest by U.S. funds capped the ringgit's rise around 2.5090.
They said the dollar could move back up to 2.5150 later in the day.
